title: Spring Framework Quick Reference
description: Look up a lesson idea, see its small example, and check a common mistake. Open the linked lesson for setup and practice steps.

entries.name: Create a managed value
entries.summary: @Bean marks a value that Spring creates. The context is a container that lets the program find that value.
notes: Close the context when the program is finished.

entries.name: Find a bean by name
entries.summary: The method name becomes the bean name. This example asks for the bean called school.
notes: The requested name must match a registered bean.

entries.name: Choose between two values
entries.summary: A container can hold several beans of one type. A name selects the one you need.
notes: A lookup by type alone is ambiguous when two beans match.

entries.name: Connect two objects
entries.summary: Spring can pass one bean into another bean method. This is dependency injection: the object receives what it needs.
notes: Declare the needed dependency instead of creating a second hidden copy.

entries.name: Share one bean instance
entries.summary: The normal Spring scope is singleton: one instance per bean definition in the container.
notes: Singleton means one per container bean definition, not one in every program everywhere.

entries.name: Ask for a fresh instance
entries.summary: Prototype scope makes a new bean each time the container is asked for it.
notes: Spring does not manage full destruction of prototype instances for you.

entries.name: Create a bean when needed
entries.summary: @Lazy delays this bean until it is requested. The print inside its factory shows when creation happens.
notes: Lazy creation delays work; it does not remove that work.

entries.name: Read a configured value
entries.summary: @Value can read a property with a fallback. No lesson.score property is set, so the fallback is 8.
notes: A fallback is used only when the property is missing.

entries.name: Run a setup method
entries.summary: initMethod names a method Spring calls after making the bean.
notes: The named method must exist and be callable with no arguments.

entries.name: Run cleanup when closing
entries.summary: destroyMethod names cleanup. Closing the context runs it for this singleton bean.
notes: Cleanup needs the context to close; an abrupt process stop may skip it.

entries.name: Choose a default bean
entries.summary: @Primary marks the preferred bean when several beans match a type.
notes: Only one matching bean should be the primary choice.

entries.name: Check whether a bean exists
entries.summary: containsBean lets code check a registered name before trying to read it.
notes: A name check does not validate every future operation on the bean.
